security_audit.summary: The confirmed risks are limited to external command execution guidance through npx @sveltejs/mcp examples and workflow steps. Several static hits are markdown fences, option names, or extension references and are false positives. No evidence of prompt injection, credential access, network exfiltration, or hidden file access was found.

remediation.suggestion: Pin @sveltejs/mcp to a reviewed version and require user confirmation before running npx commands.
State that svelte-autofixer should run only on trusted project files and within the intended workspace.
Replace MUST wording with contextual guidance so agents can skip the skill when it is not relevant.

content.user_title: Improve Svelte Code with CLI Documentation
content.value_statement: Svelte 5 syntax changes can be hard to check by memory. This skill points agents to CLI documentation and autofix commands.
actual_capabilities: Lists available Svelte 5 and SvelteKit documentation sections through @sveltejs/mcp.
Retrieves selected documentation sections for syntax and API reference.
Runs svelte-autofixer guidance against inline Svelte snippets or project files.
Supports Svelte 4 or Svelte 5 targeting through a documented option.
Reminds agents to escape Svelte rune dollar signs when using terminal input.
limitations: Requires npx access and the @sveltejs/mcp package to be available.
Does not provide standalone Svelte documentation inside the skill file.
Autofixer quality depends on the external CLI behavior and installed package version.
File analysis should be limited to trusted workspace paths.

use_cases.title: Build a Svelte 5 Component
use_cases.description: Check current rune syntax and validate a component before final delivery.

use_cases.title: Review a Svelte Migration
use_cases.description: Compare Svelte 4 and Svelte 5 behavior while reviewing migration changes.

use_cases.title: Debug SvelteKit Patterns
use_cases.description: Retrieve focused documentation sections before fixing routing, state, or component issues.

prompt_templates.title: Check Basic Syntax
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Svelte component for Svelte 5 syntax issues. Use the Svelte documentation commands before suggesting changes.

prompt_templates.title: Fetch Relevant Docs
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the Svelte documentation sections relevant to runes, derived state, and effects. Summarize what matters for this task.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a File
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the Svelte autofixer on the component file I provide. Explain each issue and propose safe fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Migration Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Svelte feature for migration risks. Use documentation lookup, target the right Svelte version, and prioritize behavior changes.

output_examples.input: A user asks for a Svelte 5 counter component review.
output_examples.output: The agent checks rune documentation, reviews the component, and reports syntax fixes with clear reasoning.

output_examples.input: A user provides a Svelte file path for debugging.
output_examples.output: The agent runs the autofixer workflow, summarizes findings, and separates required fixes from optional improvements.

output_examples.input: A team is migrating a component from Svelte 4 to Svelte 5.
output_examples.output: The agent targets the correct Svelte version, reviews migration-sensitive syntax, and explains compatibility concerns.

best_practices: Confirm the project uses Svelte before running the skill commands.
Fetch only the documentation sections needed for the current task.
Review autofixer output before changing user files.
anti_patterns: Do not run npx commands without user awareness in restricted environments.
Do not analyze files outside the intended project workspace.
Do not treat autofixer suggestions as final without human-readable review.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps agents use @sveltejs/mcp for Svelte documentation lookup and code analysis.

faq.question: Does it modify Svelte files automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill documents analysis commands and expects the agent to review results before edits.

faq.question: Which Svelte versions are covered?
faq.answer: The commands focus on Svelte 5 and include an option for targeting Svelte 4.

faq.question: Why does it mention escaping dollar signs?
faq.answer: Svelte runes use dollar signs, which shells can treat as variable markers.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should users verify before use?
faq.answer: Users should verify the npm package version and run commands only in trusted project workspaces.
